## VS Code
Visual Studio Code (VS Code) is a free, lightweight, and highly popular source-code editor developed by Microsoft. It’s designed for programmers to write, debug, and manage code efficiently across many languages.

### Key Features
#### Multi-Language Support

Works with Python, JavaScript, C++, Java, Go, Rust, HTML/CSS, and many more.

Syntax highlighting and code completion for each language.

#### Extensions & Marketplace

Thousands of extensions to add new languages, tools, and themes.

Examples: Python, GitHub Copilot, Prettier, ESLint.

#### Integrated Terminal

You can run commands directly in the editor.

Supports PowerShell, Command Prompt, bash, and others.

#### Debugging

Built-in debugger for many languages.

Can set breakpoints, inspect variables, and step through code.

#### Git & Version Control

Native integration with Git.

Commit, push, pull, and view changes without leaving the editor.

#### IntelliSense

Smart code suggestions, autocompletion, and parameter hints.

Helps you write code faster and reduce errors.

#### Cross-Platform

Runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

### Installation

Follow this link and download appropriate installer for your platform:

<https://code.visualstudio.com/>


## CircuitPython extension for VS Code 

### Key Features

#### Syntax Highlighting

* Highlights CircuitPython code (Python 3 syntax plus Adafruit-specific modules like board, digitalio, neopixel).

#### Snippets

Provides quick code snippets for common tasks:

* Controlling LEDs
* Reading sensors
* Using I2C/SPI devices
* NeoPixel strips

#### Library Awareness

Helps you see which CircuitPython libraries are used and suggests installing them into your lib folder.

#### Code Navigation

Jump to definitions and auto-complete for CircuitPython modules.

Integration with USB Drive

Works well when your board appears as CIRCUITPY:

* Quickly copy code.py to the board

* Recognizes the board type and version

Helpful Documentation

* Provides inline help for Adafruit modules.

### Installation and use

This guide explains how to install and use the CircuitPython extension for VS Code:

<https://learn.adafruit.com/using-the-circuitpython-extension-for-visual-studio-code/overview>
